page.layout: Two columns of running text, one printed page; a narrow column of marginal notes on the left margin (Drufus, Corbulo) and in the left margin near the lower part. Running head at top. Page number at top left.

main_text.p: Corbuloni, loco non decesserat. Id apud fenatum Corbulo questus, ad morem Romanorum & dignitas tem suam provocabat. pro Corbulone atas, patrius mos studia seniorum erant. ad majorum exempla, qui juventutis oblitam reverentiæ proterviam ignominiâ notaverant, animi revocabantur.
Improbitas illo fuit admirabilis ævo. Credebant hoc grande nefas, & morte piandum, Si juvenis vetulo non affurrexerit.

Contra oratores, ea ætate uberrimi, imprudentiam ætatis, & theatrorum libertatem excufabant. donec Drufus apta temperandas animis differuit, & fatisfa- ctum Corbuloni per Mamercum. qua animorum di- stractorum compositione plus favoris Drufus invenit, quàm si rigore judicis alteram partem offendisset, apud neutros stabilem fortassis gratiam initurus.
main_text.head: LXVII.
Temporis serviens conniventia juris rigore falutarior.
main_text.p: Summum jus veterum alii summam injuriam , alii summam crucem appellaverunt. Ejusrei in eodem Corbulone, gravius modo recensito, exemplum habes mus. plurima per Italiam itinera , fraude mancipum & incuria magistratuum , interruptâ & imperviâ clamitando , executioñem ejus rei libens suscepit. Quis non aut mancipum res invertas indignaretur, aut Corbulonis amantem juris animum laudaret? eventus, plurimarum retum censor, arguit. quod bau& perinde publicè ufui habitum; quàm exitiosum multis, quorum in pecuniam atque famam damnationibus & bafta favieba.
main_text.head: LXVIII.
Princeps ne in otio quidem negotium.
main_text.p: necin fecessu curam reip. deponat. Tiberius Campaniâ in peregrinatione Romano se- natu vigilantior, prævidendo pro urbe & providendo excuba-

page.notes: Left margin notes ("Drufus", "Corbulo") were read as single-word marginal references. Many words in the body are uncertain given the scan quality; several passages marked as read are best-effort and should be checked against the scan, especially the Greek-free Latin in the second column and the headings LXVII/LXVIII, which were printed as roman numerals with spacing. Two words in the first column ("bafta favieba", "perinde") are doubtful. No [?] markers were applied to these, so the text is not fully reliable.
